steps.label: Hexadecimal
steps.content:
Number Systems

Hexadecimal

Year 9, L3

steps.label: What Is Hexadecimal?
steps.content:
What Is Hexadecimal?

  • Hexadecimal ("hex") is a number system with 16 possible digits, instead of denary's 10.
  • It uses 0-9 as normal, then the letters A to F to represent the values 10 to 15.
  • Hex is used because one hex digit always represents exactly 4 bits - so a whole byte fits in just 2 hex digits, much shorter than writing out 8 bits.

steps.label: Hex Digit Values (1 of 2)

items.prompt: What denary value does the hex digit A represent?
items.explain: A is the first hex letter, worth 10.

items.prompt: What denary value does the hex digit F represent?
items.explain: F is the last hex digit, worth 15 - one less than 16 itself.

items.prompt: Which hex digit represents the denary value 13?
What denary value does the hex digit C represent?
items.explain: C is the third hex letter, worth 12.

steps.content: Hex Digit Values (1 of 2)

steps.label: Hex Digit Values (2 of 2)

items.prompt: Which hex digit represents the denary value 10?
items.explain: A is always 10 - the first letter after 9.

items.prompt: What denary value does the hex digit E represent?
items.explain: E is the fifth hex letter, worth 14.

items.prompt: Which hex digit represents the denary value 15?
items.explain: F is the highest single hex digit, worth 15.

items.prompt: What denary value does the hex digit B represent?
items.explain: B is the second hex letter, worth 11.

steps.content: Hex Digit Values (2 of 2)

steps.label: Practise Hex Digits
steps.content:
Practise Hex Digits

Before going further, get quick at recognising hex digit values - you will need this instantly, without a calculator, in every question from here on.

Steps

  1. Open Hex Quiz.
  2. Choose Level 01: Hex Digits.
  3. Answer until you can get a good run correct without pausing to think.

steps.label: Reading Hex Columns (1 of 2)

items.prompt: In the hex number 3A, which column is the digit 3 in?
items.explain: The left digit of a 2-digit hex number is always in the 16s column.

items.prompt: In the hex number 3A, which column is the digit A in?
items.explain: The right digit of a 2-digit hex number is always in the 1s column.

items.prompt: What do you multiply the LEFT digit of a 2-digit hex number by?
items.explain: The left digit is worth its value x16.

steps.content: Reading Hex Columns (1 of 2)

steps.label: Reading Hex Columns (2 of 2)

items.prompt: What do you multiply the RIGHT digit of a 2-digit hex number by?
items.explain: The right digit is worth its value x1, so it never changes.

items.prompt: How many hex digits are needed to represent one whole byte (8 bits)?
items.explain: Each hex digit is exactly 4 bits, so a byte (8 bits) needs 2 hex digits.

items.prompt: Denary's columns are worth 1 and 10. What are hex's two columns worth?
items.explain: Hex is base 16, so its columns go up in powers of 16: 1, then 16.

steps.content: Reading Hex Columns (2 of 2)
